title: Before the Next Rollout: Diagnosing Skill Utility Shifts from Policy Updates
abstract: arXiv:2610.39358v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Skill-evolution methods typically analyze execution trajectories to guide agent skill refinement. However, policy updates can change the behavioral effects and marginal utility of an unchanged skill. Attribution based on earlier trajectories may therefore no longer reflect the skill's contribution under the updated policy. Moreover, trajectory failures can arise from multiple factors, making individual skill contributions difficult to isolate. We evaluate whether policy-update signals contain predictive information about changes in skill marginal utility. At fixed contexts from pre-update training rollouts, we measure how policy updates change the contrast in token preferences between skill and control conditions. Combining these interaction shifts with advantage estimates yields reward-directed readouts for diagnosing utility changes. translated_title: 在下一次部署之前：从策略更新中诊断技能效用的变化
translated_abstract: 技能演化方法通常通过分析执行轨迹来指导智能体技能的改进。然而，策略更新可能会改变一个本身未变的技能的行为效果和边际效用。因此，基于早期轨迹的归因可能不再反映该技能在更新后策略下的贡献。此外，轨迹失败可能由多种因素引起，使得单个技能的贡献难以被隔离。我们评估了策略更新信号是否包含关于技能边际效用变化的预测信息。在来自更新前训练轨迹的固定上下文中，我们测量策略更新如何改变技能条件与控制条件之间token偏好的对比。将这些交互变化与优势估计相结合，可以得到用于诊断效用变化的奖励导向读出信号。这些读出信号复用现有的训练轨迹，且对于单步动作选择只需进行前向传播计算。
tldr: 该论文提出一种在策略更新后、下一次部署前诊断技能效用变化的方法，通过测量策略更新对技能条件与控制条件间token偏好对比的影响，并结合优势估计构建奖励导向读出信号，仅复用现有训练轨迹和前向传播即可预测技能边际效用的变化。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes diagnosing skill utility shifts after policy updates before the next rollout by measuring how updates alter the contrast in token preferences between skill and control conditions, combining these interaction shifts with advantage estimates to yield reward-directed readouts that reuse existing training rollouts and require only forward passes.
